name: Lidar Obstacle-Avoidance & Line-Following Rover
one_liner: A four-wheel rover that maps obstacles with lidar and follows lines on its own.
intro: A four-wheel rover platform with lidar, line tracking and several autonomous driving modes. The team built the device-side software, the controller board architecture, chose and tuned the chassis, and debugged the full system. It is meant for robotics teaching, algorithm testing, indoor inspection and demos.

tech_stack.value: STM32F103RCT6

tech_stack.label: Sensors
tech_stack.value: Lidar, line-tracking sensors, MPU6050 IMU, wheel encoders, ultrasonic sensor port

tech_stack.label: Drive
tech_stack.value: 4-wheel chassis, DC motors with dual encoded motor-driver ports

tech_stack.label: Control
tech_stack.value: PID closed-loop speed control; modes for manual/app control, lidar avoidance, lidar follow, wall following, CCD and electromagnetic line tracking

tech_stack.label: Wireless
tech_stack.value: Bluetooth module for app / remote control

tech_stack.label: Power
tech_stack.value: 6–16 V DC input, 5 V 5 A output, voltage monitor

tech_stack.label: Interfaces
tech_stack.value: Display port, buzzer, SWD debug, USB download, reserved serial port

scope: Device-side software: embedded control, drivers and application logic
Controller board architecture: sensors, motor drive and power design

Lidar data acquisition and processing
Obstacle-avoidance algorithm with real-time perception and path planning

Motor driver design with encoder feedback and protection
Functional testing, performance tuning and demo

name: Bionic Hexapod Robot
